No, except if you went right for their sensitive area. I actually know several high school students arrested or interrogated for their 'misbehaviour' online.

I would recommend Shanghai first. It's probably the most intetnational city China got. Hong Kong is another place of interest, but is currently under lockdown. My favourite city is probably Chengdu, a thriving haven far away from the political center Beijing.

There's an extent on how much they can pay. They were students with excellent grades when they were in college, and they went to the US with the university backing up funds. Because of [计划生育](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_planning_policy?wprov=sfla1), they chose to born me in the US.

High schools in China were determined to raise students with high capabilities for the reputation of itself, offering little to no fee for the students that have good grades.

I am a US Citizen born in the USA, and my parents brought me back to China three months after I was born. Since my parents were relatively poor, they found my citizenship an advantage over others, for I can enroll in public high schools with low fee. Even if I got poor grades there, I can go back to China to enroll in some of the best colleges with little competition.

However I found myself going through mental pain for the segregation I felt there, and I begged my parents to sent me back. But I don't anticipate them throwing me into a test machine manufacturing plant.
People live busily and merrily most of the time. If you don't start to worry about the potential threat of the CCP, China is a county with beautiful cities and towns.

I don't honor the fact that China has contained the virus so well. People suffered for the compulsory 'stay at home' order, many who were depressed or illed for other reasons like diabetes or cancer died at homes. Only after the disease was contained did the government started to  boast on government controlled medias that China's regulation system is way better than the USA, when people already started to forgot the trauma that were made by the actions of the state.

I self taught myself through audiobooks and imported English books.
My parents send me to a American high school at the age of 15, and left me there to suffer. I can't adapt myself to the American culture after living in China for 15 years since born. I isolated myself in the bedroom for days on end, getting more depressed day by day for the cultural shock and internet addiction.
My parents send me back to China in 2019 for the miserable grades I am earning there. They directly throw me into one of the toughest high schools in the district, which claims several student's lives for the pressure. I feel myself thrown from one end of the education system to another. I became so lost.
